answer: In an AI-agent economy, sybil resistance can come from requiring each agent to continuously prove unique behavioral provenance through ongoing attestation of its decision history, creating a velvet-smooth chain of verifiable actions that a hollow mass of fake identities cannot cheaply replicate. An attacker must bear the umber cost of generating and sustaining distinct, non-copyable interaction traces for every duplicate, which scales linearly with the number of sybils and quickly exceeds any gain from flooding the network.
